title: Design Security, Compliance, and Governance
objective: Place controls at the boundaries of organizations, accounts, identities, data, and networks.

sections.title: Using Multi-Account as a Responsibility Boundary
paragraphs: In a multi-account environment, design accounts not merely as billing units, but as boundaries that separate workloads, environments, data classifications, and operational responsibilities. Define which operations are prohibited across the organization, which operations are delegated within each account, where logs are centralized, and the approval path for exceptions.

Governance does not end with organization policies. Combine identity federation, least-privilege roles, permissions boundaries, resource policies, and continuous configuration monitoring to track who can perform which operations on which resources in which accounts, and under what conditions.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Security, Compliance, and Governance

sections.title: Mapping Identity to Data Boundaries
paragraphs: Architects distinguish human sign-ins, application execution roles, and temporary credentials for external systems. For cross-account access, they verify the trust policy, permissions policy, external ID, and session conditions, and they do not use broadly shared credentials.

For data protection, they align encryption at rest and in transit, the principals allowed to use the keys, key rotation and deletion protection, and audit logs with the data classification. Even when encryption is enabled, the boundary is not protected if decryption permissions or backup restoration permissions are too broad.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Identity and Key Management

sections.title: Detecting Configuration Drift and Remediating It Safely
paragraphs: Compliance requirements do not remain effective simply because they are written in a design document. Define the target resources, desired configurations, the rationale for exceptions, expiration dates, detection methods, and remediation approvers, and retain the history of configuration changes and evaluation results.

AWS Config provides information for reviewing resource configurations, relationships between resources, and configuration history. Design automatic remediation with narrowly defined targets, execution permissions, impact scope, stop conditions, and recovery procedures so that it does not unconditionally overwrite even approved exceptions.

checkpoints.prompt: An organization operating production workloads across multiple business divisions wants to separate operational permissions and audit scope between divisions. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: All business divisions use a single shared administrator user.
choices.explanation: This eliminates principal identification and least privilege.

choices.text: Store logs only on each operator’s local device.
choices.explanation: This cannot ensure organization-wide auditing or tamper resistance.

choices.text: Separate accounts as responsibility boundaries, and combine federation, least-privilege roles, organization policies, and centralized logging.
choices.explanation: This enables governance while separating responsibilities, permissions, and audit trails.

checkpoints.prompt: An automated process operated by an external contractor needs to write temporarily to an S3 bucket in a specific account. Which access design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Share long-term access keys among multiple contractors.
choices.explanation: Tracking the principal and managing revocation become difficult.

choices.text: Create a cross-account IAM role limited to the required operations and bucket, and verify the trust conditions and external ID.
choices.explanation: Temporary credentials and limited permissions make it possible to identify the external principal.

checkpoints.prompt: I want to automatically remediate an S3 bucket only when it has a tag that prohibits public access but is configured for public access. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Overwrite the settings of every bucket every minute, regardless of the reason.
choices.explanation: This could damage approved exceptions or changes currently in operation.

choices.text: Delete only the public-access notification without retaining the configuration history.
choices.explanation: This prevents investigation of the cause and prevention of recurrence.

choices.text: Design remediation that evaluates the target tag and desired configuration and includes exception approval, a least-privilege remediation role, execution logging, and stop conditions.
choices.explanation: This safely remediates only the necessary targets with an audit trail.
